name: Kaveri Seed Company Ltd
title: Kaveri Seed Company Ltd - 532899 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Kaveri built inventory 17% y/y on purpose, mgmt says prices may not rise in FY27 and revenue growth should be 15-20% on volume; channel and company inventories both high, a supply-side caution.

triggers.label: Inventory up 17% vs sales 16%

triggers.label: No price hikes expected in FY27
triggers.quote: we may not be able to increase the prices, like how we have increased last year

triggers.label: Revenue growth 15-20% FY27
triggers.quote: Overall, the revenue should be in between the 15% to 20% growth.

triggers.label: Cotton new hybrids 10.3% → 30.05%
triggers.quote: Contribution for new cotton hybrids improved significantly, increasing from 10.3% to 30.05%

guidance.quote: Overall, the revenue should be in between the 15% to 20% growth.
But in cotton, it should be more than 20-odd percent.

red_flags.quote: we have received INR75 crores to INR80 crores of lower advances

red_flags.quote: So the inventory levels are pretty high in the system, especially with the companies.

red_flags.quote: In Gujarat, it's still continuing as of now.

evasions.quote: Not really, but the sentiment of the farmers or the cash flow is a bit tight across the channels.
So we may not worry about the write-offs

summary.headline: Kaveri Seed FY26 revenue rose 16.25% to INR 1,303.77 crore, but PAT grew only 6.8% to INR 283.26 crore; management guides FY27 revenue growth of 15-20%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations rose 6.84% YoY to INR 82.21 crore and the net loss narrowed to INR 25.65 crore from INR 29.25 crore. For FY26, revenue grew 16.25% to INR 1,303.77 crore, EBITDA rose 8.34% to INR 349.75 crore, and PAT rose 6.8% to INR 283.26 crore. Growth came from maize, hybrid rice, selection rice, exports and new cotton hybrids. Management said inventory is elevated by design, with higher yields and a deliberate buffer, and that FY27 growth will be volume-led because price increases are unlikely.

financial_highlights.change: +6.84% YoY vs INR 76.95 crore in Q4 FY25
vs net loss of INR 29.25 crore in Q4 FY25

financial_highlights.value: approx. +90% FY26; nearly +76% in Q4 FY26

financial_highlights.change: down from INR 600 crore last year (per analyst); management cited INR 75-80 crore lower customer advances

segments.name: Cotton
segments.commentary: New hybrids rose to 30.05% of cotton contribution from 10.3%. Management expects cotton to grow faster than the company, above 20% in a good case, driven by new hybrids across North, Central and South India.

segments.name: Maize
segments.commentary: FY26 volume grew 18.84% and revenue 40.17%, the key growth driver. Kharif outlook is flat-to-sideways due to sentiment and fertiliser shortfall; rabi is seen as positive.

segments.name: Rice
segments.commentary: Hybrid rice revenue rose 18.3% despite Punjab restrictions; selection rice revenue rose 9.76%. Growth is expected from Punjab, UP, Bihar, Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: FY26 exports grew about 90% and Q4 FY26 exports grew about 76%; management expects strong performance to continue.

segments.name: Rainy millet
segments.commentary: Growth expected in Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh; no figures were given.

guidance_outlook: FY27 overall revenue growth guided at 15-20%, with upside to above 15% at company level.
Cotton growth expected above 20% in a good case and to outpace the company average.
Price increases unlikely in FY27, so revenue growth should track volume growth.
Margins expected to improve in FY27 as production cost per unit is slightly lower on higher yields and other costs fall; gross margin may expand from about 47% (peak 49.5% cited by analyst).
Buyback not planned now; management said it would revisit in 3-5 months once inventory cash is realised. Dividend is typically one-time, paid in Q2 or Q3.
capex_capacity: Capital work in progress is INR 99 crore standalone and INR 129 crore consolidated; capex covers land, office buildings, plant and machinery and a seed processing unit.
Only about INR 30 crore of capex relates to one building under construction; land purchases are for R&D.
Inventory rose about 17% YoY (management later said 15-18%) by deliberate production to hold buffer stock; yields were 5-7% higher.
BG-III trait approval: no concrete update, moving slowly.
demand_pricing: Industry inventory is high across cotton, maize and rice, mostly held at companies ahead of the season; placements have only just started in some areas.
Price increases are unlikely this year due to high inventory and farmer cash-flow stress; company has not pushed advances because margins have shrunk.
Illegal BT cotton is still present in Gujarat; management says it sees no rise elsewhere and does not compete with it.
Monsoon: early pre-monsoon showers reported; management says a delay could shift cropping patterns, which the product mix can offset.
Seeds Bill expected to be notified soon, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory rise about 17% when sales grew about 16%, and will the buffer persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Production was raised on purpose to hold buffer stock amid last year's competition for production areas; yields of 5-7% higher also added to inventory. Management said inventory is not a concern.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other current liabilities and customer advances fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Advances were INR 75-80 crore lower YoY because farmer cash flows are tight and the company has not pushed advances, which would require higher incentives, as margins have shrunk.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 growth be driven by volume or price, and what margin is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth will be volume-led with no price hikes; revenue guided at 15-20%, cotton above 20%. Lower production costs and stable other costs should lift margins; management did not give a specific margin figure.

qa_highlights.question: Are write-offs a risk on older cotton seed inventory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most inventory is new production with about 1.3-1.5 years of age against a 3-year cotton seed life, so write-off risk is low and any leftover stock will be used next year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for maize in kharif, given high channel inventory and El Nino?
qa_highlights.answer: Kharif sentiment is weak, with sideways trend tied to El Nino uncertainty and fertiliser shortage; rabi is positive, and the company expects to grow in kharif by targeting new pockets.

qa_highlights.question: How are the Kaveri and Aditya brands positioned?
qa_highlights.answer: Aditya and Genomix are wholly owned subsidiaries that market B2B hybrids from R&D; Kaveri focuses on its main product line, and the subsidiaries sell different products but may compete among themselves.

risks_watch: High industry inventory across cotton, maize and rice could pressure pricing and force channel discounts.
Tax litigation: company claims seed income as agricultural income; management said it has won at Commissioner (Appeals) level and that no other litigation is currently pending.
Monsoon/El Nino uncertainty and fertiliser shortage could hurt kharif maize and cropping patterns.
Illegal BT cotton continues in Gujarat.
Higher gross margin depends on cost reductions passing through without price increases.
Watch Q1 FY27 for maize kharif sales, cotton hybrid growth, and inventory and advance trends.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume growth and new cotton hybrids, but cautious on pricing, citing high industry inventory and farmer cash-flow stress. Evasive on the BG-III trait approval and on the specific margin target.
key_quotes: Most of the growth what we anticipate this year should come from the new products, so that we have already seen the initial trend last year.
This year, we may not be able to increase the prices, like how we have increased last year, but other than that, the production cost is also slightly lower than last year.
The inventory is higher in all 3 crops. In all 3 crops, the inventory is higher.

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth guided at 15-20% (midpoint 17.5%), with cotton expected above 20%, but no specific new capacity, order book figures or contracts were quantified and management said price increases are unlikely, so volume growth must come from demand and share gains; backing is partial.
